html:
A battle on 22 April 1900 near Kousseri, on the Chari River across from today's N'Djamena, where three French columns defeated and killed the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr.

Rabih, a slave trader from Sudan, had conquered Bagirmi and Bornu in the 1890s. The French sent columns from Algeria, the Congo and the Niger, which met at Lake Chad. Rabih was killed, and so was the French commander, Major Amedee-Francois Lamy, who gave his name to the new post of Fort-Lamy, now N'Djamena. The battle marked the start of French rule over Chad, which joined French Equatorial Africa.
